description: Tests whether adding low-frequency macro variables to a GARCH model improves daily volatility forecasting for SPY. Variants: VIX (daily), yield curve TNX (daily), monthly realized variance. Benchmark: GJR-GARCH(1,1).

specification.long_run: τ_t = m + θ × Σ φ_k(w1,w2) × X_{t-k}

hypothesis: VIX already incorporates macro information → GARCH-MIDAS with true macro variables should be null
conclusion_detail: True macro variables (yield curve, monthly RV) are NULL or significantly WORSE than GJR-GARCH. VIX as MIDAS driver shows significant improvement (DM t=-3.87, p=0.0001), but VIX is itself a volatility measure — not an external macro variable. This confirms VIX sufficient statistic hypothesis: VIX contains incremental vol information beyond GARCH, but no true macro variable does.

midas_vix_daily.caveat: VIX is a volatility measure, not a true macro variable. This result confirms VIX contains incremental info beyond GARCH, consistent with 12/VIX VT outperforming GARCH-VT (J3/J13).

midas_yield_curve_daily.note: Significantly WORSE than GJR (positive DM-t = GJR better). Yield curve adds noise, not signal.

midas_monthly_rv.note: Significantly WORSE than GJR (positive DM-t = GJR better). Monthly RV is too low-frequency; GARCH persistence already captures this. Confirms K51 MF2-GARCH null.

interpretation.main_finding: For true macro variables (yield curve, monthly RV), GARCH-MIDAS is NULL or even harmful — they are significantly WORSE than standard GJR-GARCH. Only VIX as MIDAS driver improves forecasting, but VIX is a market-derived volatility measure, not an external macro variable.
interpretation.vix_sufficient_statistic: MIDAS-VIX improvement (QLIKE -8.304 vs -8.256, DM p=0.0001) confirms VIX contains incremental volatility information beyond what GARCH captures from returns alone. This is consistent with J3/J4/J8/J13: VIX is a sufficient statistic. The GARCH-MIDAS framework with VIX is effectively another way to incorporate VIX into vol forecasting — similar to 12/VIX VT but through model structure rather than trading rule.
interpretation.macro_null_confirmed: Yield curve (TNX) and monthly realized variance both significantly WORSEN forecasting. This confirms: (1) K51 MF2-GARCH null extends to external macro variables, (2) GARCH persistence (alpha+beta+gamma/2 ~ 0.97, half-life ~23 days) already captures slow-moving vol, (3) monthly data is too low-frequency to add signal at daily horizon.
interpretation.why_macro_hurts: Adding macro variables actually HURTS by introducing estimation noise. The MIDAS Beta polynomial weights (w1, w2) add 4 extra parameters that need estimation. When the signal is weak (macro variables), the noise from estimating these parameters dominates any marginal information gain.
interpretation.practical_implication: For practitioners: (1) VIX is sufficient for daily vol forecasting — no need to look at macro fundamentals, (2) If using VIX in a model, simple rules (12/VIX) work as well as complex MIDAS structures, (3) The only remaining frontier for improvement is intraday data (HAR-RV, Realized GARCH).
